name: Estuary / delta
notes: Brackish tidal river mouths and deltas: cordgrass and glasswort marsh fringing mudflats, reed and bulrush beds on the fresher side, mangrove in tropical deltas, and eelgrass in the channels. Drawn on Atlantic North America (Chesapeake), NW Europe (Wadden Sea, Thames), the Mekong/Ganges deltas and SE Australian estuaries; underwater species flagged.

canopy.name: Crack willow
canopy.source: Salix fragilis (S. x fragilis), European tidal river banks and freshwater deltas, 10-20 m — Wikipedia

traits.leaf_shape: simple or compound broad leaves, most deciduous in cold bands
traits.trunk: single trunk dividing into a rounded crown
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.note: grey-brown, thick, deeply fissured into a criss-cross network of ridges

canopy.silhouette: broad ragged dome on short forked trunk, brittle limbs

growth.juvenile_note: Spreads mostly by twigs that snap off cleanly at the base (the 'crack'), float downstream and root on banks within 1-2 weeks; true seedlings are rare (2 tiny round cotyledons). The young tree is a fast whip with long, glossy, lance-shaped leaves, soon forking into several ascending stems; old trees split, lean and fall, and fallen limbs resprout in a line.
growth.source: Stace, New Flora of the British Isles, and Meikle (BSBI) for form, 10-25 m size and vegetative spread; USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual Salix (willow seed has no dormancy and germinates within 12-24 h on wet ground (USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual Salix)); growth, first seed and lifespan estimated for a fast, short-lived riverside willow

fruiting.source: Stace and Meikle (BSBI): catkins with the leaves Apr-May, males 2-5 cm, females 3-7 cm, glabrous capsules ~4-5 mm; many stands are single-sex clones so seed set is often poor; ripening, fruit set and crop estimated from other tree willows

traits.trunk: prop roots or pneumatophores over mud
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.note: smooth pale grey to whitish, flaking in thin patches to greenish under-bark

canopy.silhouette: low grey-green dome over a field of pencil roots

growth.juvenile_note: Cryptoviviparous: the pale grey-green, heart-shaped propagule falls, sheds its skin within days and opens two thick fleshy cotyledons while hairy roots anchor it in the mud. The seedling is a slim stem with opposite, glossy green leaves that are silvery-grey beneath; pencil-like pneumatophores soon ring the young tree, which branches low into a bushy shrub.
growth.source: Almahasheer et al. 2016 Sci. Rep. 6:37785 (Red Sea growth: ~9.6 nodes/yr, internodes 5-11 cm/yr); Duke 1990 J. Ecol. (latitudinal phenology); seedling-bank behaviour from Australian studies; height-growth timings, first flowering and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: Almahasheer et al. 2016 Sci. Rep. (Red Sea: buds from June, peak flowering Nov, propagules ~3 months after flowering, released by April); Duke 1990 (flowering-to-fruit-fall lengthens with latitude, to ~1 yr in temperate Australia/NZ); propagules eaten after soaking/roasting; fruit set and crop estimated.

canopy.name: Nipa palm
canopy.source: Nypa fruticans, SE Asian and Bay of Bengal deltas (Mekong, Sundarbans), trunkless palm in brackish tidal mud, 4-9 m — Wikipedia

traits.leaf_shape: fan or feather fronds in a terminal crown
traits.trunk: single unbranched columnar trunk (doum forks; clumpers sucker)
traits.petiole: long fibrous petiole with a leaf sheath
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.note: trunkless: prostrate rhizome with massive green petiole bases

canopy.silhouette: trunkless fountain of erect feather fronds from mud

growth.juvenile_note: The seed often starts growing while the fibrous fruit is still on the head or drifting on the tide: a pointed shoot pokes out and the stranded seedling roots in soft estuary mud. First leaves are short, with few broad leaflets; then ever bigger, erect, feather-shaped fronds up to 9 m rise straight from a forking stem that creeps buried in the mud, so the palm never shows a trunk.
growth.source: Wikipedia Nypa fruticans (stem grows beneath the ground; leaves to 9 m; seeds may germinate while water-borne); PROSEA Nypa (flowering starts a few years after planting, tapped for sap from ~5 yr); seedling leaf form and ages estimated

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (flowers all year; globular head of female flowers with catkin-like red or yellow male branches below; pollinated by small insects incl. Drosophila flies, bees, beetles; woody fruit head to 25+ cm, up to 30 kg, breaks up into floating fibrous fruits; young seeds edible); fruit size, set and timing estimated

traits.native_range: Casuarina glauca, E Australian estuary margins behind mangroves, needle-like branchlets, 8-20 m — Wikipedia

traits.trunk: single straight trunk, whorled branches, conical crown
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: true leaves are whorls of minute scale teeth; the drooping glaucous branchlets are drawn as needles

bark.note: hard grey-brown bark, scaly and longitudinally fissured

canopy.silhouette: narrow dark spire of drooping grey-green threads

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling like other she-oaks: two small cotyledons then whorls of minute scale leaves on jointed grey-green twigs, growing into a narrow cone. Established trees throw up root suckers all around, so a swamp-oak stand is a dense thicket of slender stems of many ages from one clone.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree C. glauca (8-20 m, moderately fast, avg 5 m at 7 yr on trial sites, dioecious, vigorous root suckers throughout life, mature cones 9-18 x 7-9 mm, ~415,000 seeds/kg); germination and first cones from Casuarina accounts (PROSEA)

fruiting.source: ICRAF Agroforestree C. glauca (dioecious, young female cones 3-12 mm, mature cones 9-18 x 7-9 mm); flowering season and cone maturation estimated from C. equisetifolia (PROSEA, 18-20 weeks) and SE Australian flora notes

shrub.name: Groundsel bush
shrub.source: Baccharis halimifolia, SE US and Gulf estuary margins (invasive in Australia/Europe), fluffy white seed heads, 1-4 m — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: Baccharis halimifolia, SE US and Gulf estuary margins (invasive in Australia/Europe), fluffy white seed heads, 1-4 m — W

bark.note: grey-brown, shallowly fissured on old stems; young twigs green and angled

shrub.silhouette: loose rounded bush, white fluff crown in autumn

growth.juvenile_note: Wind-blown achenes sprout on bare, damp ground within 1-3 weeks. The seedling has two small oval cotyledons, then thick, grey-green, coarsely toothed, wedge-shaped leaves on a single stem that branches in its first year; the young plant is an upright, leafy, many-branched bush, often flowering in its second autumn.
growth.source: Wikipedia (to 4 m, dioecious, snowy-white cottony female heads in autumn, nectar for butterflies including monarchs, seeds toxic); weed-management literature (Queensland, CABI) on quick light-dependent germination, flowering from year 2 and seed output; lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (autumn flowering, female heads become snowy-white tufts, seeds toxic); weed literature (a large female bush sheds up to ~1.5 million plumed achenes); heads-per-plant, fruit set and timings estimated. Counts are flower heads.

shrub.silhouette: upright leafy bush of many straight stems

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings come up in spring along the upper marsh edge and wrack line: a slender stem with pairs of thick, fleshy, toothed, lance-shaped leaves. It grows quickly into a many-branched, semi-woody shrub whose upper branches carry leafy spikes of small, nodding, greenish-white flower heads in late summer.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Iva frutescens: shrub to 3.5 m, many small heads with whitish florets, narrow band at the upper salt-marsh margin, growth limited by flooding); wind pollination as in other Iva; timings estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (elongated arrays of many small whitish heads); Iva heads are wind-pollinated and set small dark obovoid achenes shed through autumn and winter (timings, set and crop estimated).

bark.note: procumbent woody stems, pale grey-brown, finely fissured; silvery-mealy young shoots

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings on bare salt-marsh mud have two narrow fleshy cotyledons and then small, opposite, mealy silver-grey leaves. Branches sprawl and root where they touch the mud, so within a few years one plant becomes a low, dense, silvery-grey evergreen hummock lining creeks, with small elliptic scurfy leaves and short spikes of tiny yellowish flowers.
growth.source: Biological Flora of the British Isles: Halimione portulacoides (Chapman 1950); salt-marsh ecology accounts (spreads by layering, wind-pollinated, fruits float on tides). Values estimated.

fruiting.source: Floras and Chapman 1950 (tiny wind-pollinated flowers Jul-Sep in short terminal panicled spikes; fruit enclosed in 3-lobed flattened bracteoles 2.5-5 mm, ripe Sep-Nov and carried by tides). Counts and timings estimated.

bark.note: stout yellow-green culms; pale straw nodes and sheaths

ground.silhouette: stiff yellow-green cordgrass sward, culms all one height

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a stiff single shoot with flat, grey-green, sharply pointed leaves; it tillers and sends short rhizomes so each seedling becomes a round tussock widening up to 30 cm a year, and tussocks merge into a dense sward within one to two decades. Culms live about a year; old swards may die back after decades.
growth.source: IUCN GISD and NOBANIS fact sheets (seed viable only one season, 0.6-5% viable; tussock radial growth up to 30 cm/yr; flowers Jul-Oct, seed ripens in ~12 weeks; 0.3-1.3 m); Gray et al. 1991 ITE Spartina anglica research review (germination faster at 20 C, marsh die-back from the 1920s)

traits.native_range: Phragmites australis, cosmopolitan, brackish upper estuary and delta reedbeds (Danube, Rhone), 2-4 m — Wikipedia

bark.note: tall hollow culms, green then straw, standing dead through winter

ground.silhouette: tall even reed wall with feathery plumed tops

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are small, weak, grass-like tufts of soft green leaves on wet mud. After a season rhizomes and long surface runners spread out; every spring new culms shoot up like thin canes to full height in a few months, with long, broad, grey-green leaves all along the stem and a big, silky, purple-brown plume that fades to grey-buff.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Phragmites australis (germination needs light, moisture and warm alternating temperatures after cold stratification; seedling survival very low; 3-4 years to viable seed; maximum height at 5-8 years; no part of a clone lives more than 8 years though clones persist far longer; culms die back yearly)

ground.name: Eelgrass
ground.origin: North Atlantic and North Pacific coasts
ground.source: underwater — Zostera marina, N Hemisphere estuary and lagoon channels on sand/mud, ribbon-leaved seagrass 0.3-1.2 m — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: underwater — Zostera marina, N Hemisphere estuary and lagoon channels on sand/mud, ribbon-leaved seagrass 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.note: submerged; leaves sheathed on a creeping rhizome

ground.silhouette: submerged meadow of long green ribbons streaming with tide

growth.juvenile_note: The seed splits and a white seedling axis anchors in sandy mud; a green cotyledon is followed by 2-3 narrow, flat, bright green ribbon leaves from a sheath. The seedling soon grows a creeping white rhizome with roots at each node and new shoots along it, so a first-year plant is a short row of leafy tufts; leaf length (a few cm to over 1 m) depends on water depth and clarity.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Zostera marina): leaves to 1.2 cm wide and over 1 m long (a few cm in clear shallow water), perennial but may grow as an annual, several thousand seeds per m2, inflorescence about 10 cm, one meadow clone about 3000 years old. Germination, seedling growth, flowering age and shoot life estimated from eelgrass restoration studies.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling with 2 fleshy, finger-like green cotyledons, then a leafless, jointed, succulent green stem (the tiny leaves are fused into the segments) that branches into a little candelabra 10-30 cm tall. Flowers hide in the joints late in summer; the whole plant turns red or purple in autumn, sheds seed and dies.
growth.source: Davy, Bishop & Costa 2001, Biological Flora of the British Isles: Salicornia (spring germination on the marsh after rain lowers salinity, flowering Aug-Sep, seed shed in autumn, strictly annual); Wikipedia S. europaea (shoots harvested Jun-Aug, turns red/purple in autumn, edible)

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds need winter cold and sprout in spring on wet, bare mud. The seedling is a grass-like tuft of narrow, keeled leaves; by late summer it sends out rhizomes that swell into walnut-sized tubers, from which next year's stout, sharply three-angled stems rise to 1 m or more, topped by a cluster of chunky brown spikelets over long leafy bracts.
growth.source: Wikipedia (saline, muddy, mineral-rich wetlands flooded in spring; near-cosmopolitan); general Bolboschoenus biology (seeds need stratification; shoots die back yearly; tuber chains perennate a few years; clones persist for decades); timings estimated. lifespan_years is the tuber-ramet.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: two small oval cotyledons, then a low rosette of fleshy, hairless, strap-shaped leaves with faint parallel veins, lying on the salt-marsh mud. growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: one soft shoot with flat, tapering, bright-green leaves; it tillers within weeks and sends out rhizomes, reaching ~15 cm in 3-4 months. ground.name: Widgeongrass

traits.native_range: underwater — Ruppia maritima, worldwide brackish estuary shallows, thread-leaved submerged plant 20-80 cm — Wikipedia

ground.silhouette: hazy tangle of thread stems just below the surface

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling a thread-fine shoot with hair-like leaves. Grows into a loose underwater tuft of slender, much-branched stems with alternate, very narrow leaves 2-10 cm long sheathed at the base, from a thin creeping rhizome; tiny flowers reach the surface and leave clusters of small beaked fruits on stalks. Often dies back and restarts from seed each year.
growth.source: Flora of N America and Kantrud 1991 'Wigeongrass: a literature review' (USFWS): submerged annual-or-perennial of brackish water, spring germination, flowers and fruits within a few months, often regrows from seed each year; timings estimated from those accounts
